title: local-inference-adapter-runtime-scratchpad
content:
Purpose: quick brain dump for a tiny local adapter runtime so devs can run multi-model/multi-session inference locally without requiring full Redwood Dedicated or Private. This is a personal scratchpad — not final.

Goals (hand-wavy):
- single binary that exposes a subset of Redwood API locally (text-gen, chat, embeddings) and can route to: local model files, dockerized containers, or remote hosted endpoints (with token passthrough).
- session multiplexing so multiple apps can share a single dev GPU while keeping KV caches isolated.
- lightweight config so product teams can prototype end-to-end quickly.

Key constraints / non-goals:
- Not aimed at production security or multi-tenant isolation (just dev comfort).
- Should run on a laptop + external GPU or small dev VM. No heavy autoscaling.

High-level components (conceptual):
- CLI / daemon: rw-locald (runs as user service)
- Local adapter API (HTTP) that mirrors a small piece of Redwood hosted API surface (for minimal integration testing)
- Session manager: creates per-session contexts (KV cache dirs, quantization params) and enforces memory/slot quotas
- Router: maps incoming requests to target backend (local-llm, docker-run, remote-proxy)
- Persistence: optional per-session KV cache on disk to speed up repeated dev cycles

ASCII diagram (very rough):

[app] -> HTTP -> rw-locald API -> SESSION MGR -> ROUTER -> {local-llm | docker-container | remote-hosted}
                                  |
                                  -> disk KV cache (~/rw-locald/sessions/<id>/kv)

API shape draft (trimmed, emulate Redwood hosted minimal subset):

POST /v1/local/sessions  # create session
Request JSON:
{
  "owner": "string",           # optional, e.g. dev email
  "model": "path-or-name",    # local path or short name like gptq-vicuna-7b
  "backend": "local|docker|remote",
  "memory_limit_mb": 8192,
  "quantize": "int8|int4|none",
  "cache_persist": true
}
Response JSON:
{
  "session_id": "uuid",
  "endpoint": "/v1/local/run/<session_id>",
  "kv_path": "~/rw-locald/sessions/<uuid>/kv"
}

POST /v1/local/run/<session_id>
Request JSON (text gen):
{
  "input": "string or list of tokens",
  "max_tokens": 256,
  "temperature": 0.2,
  "top_p": 0.95,
  "stream": false
}
Response JSON:
{
  "id": "req-uuid",
  "output": "string",
  "tokens": ["..."],
  "usage": {"input_tokens": "int", "output_tokens": "int"}
}

Design notes on API shape: keep HTTP/JSON only to avoid heavy deps for devs. Stream via SSE for streaming responses. We intentionally avoid full function-calling API in first pass.

Session multiplexing model:
- Each session has a token budget and a memory budget. The daemon tracks GPU memory usage per backend process.
- Simple policy: round-robin on active sessions up to concurrency N (configurable), evict LRU KV caches if memory pressure high.
- For local-file models, we allow multiple sessions to share same loaded model if quantization/config matches. Sharing rules: identical model path + identical quantize flag -> share single process with multiplexed requests; otherwise spawn separate process.

Config sketch (CLI flags + YAML):
- rw-locald --config ~/.rw-locald/config.yaml
Example config.yaml:
daemon_port: 14000
max_gpu_mem_mb: 32768
session_defaults:
  memory_limit_mb: 8192
  quantize: int8
backends:
  local_models_dir: ~/models
  docker_socket: unix:///var/run/docker.sock
  remote_proxy_base: https://api.redwood.ai
logging: debug

Security (minimal):
- Local-only by default (127.0.0.1). If bind_all true, warn user.
- Token passthrough for remote-proxy requests (read from env REDWOOD_API_KEY)
- Optional per-session secret for sharing sessions with teammates (dev-only).

Performance considerations / heuristics:
- Pre-warm model on session create if memory available (avoid O(10s) first call).
- Persistent KV cache per session (fast resume), store index of cached prefixes. Add eviction TTL (e.g., 7d).
- For small sequences prefer synchronous path, for >512 tokens prefer batched async worker.

Persistence layout (disk):
~/.rw-locald/
  sessions/
    <uuid>/
      kv.bin
      config.json
      logs/
  models/  -> symlinks to ~/models/ or downloaded artifacts

Open questions / TODOs (priority rough):
- Q: Should session create be idempotent if same owner+model+config? (avoid duplicate loads)  -> probably yes, return existing if cached.
- Q: How to handle incompatible quantize/share rules? Best-effort convert or force spawn?  -> spawn separate process to avoid falling into conversion complexity.
- Q: UX for streaming in local tests (SSE vs websockets)?  -> SSE simpler to implement in daemon.
- TODO: sketch health endpoint for each backend process (pid, mem usage, loaded_model_id).
- TODO: implement a tiny shim that translates Redwood SDK calls to local endpoints for 0-change app testing (python/js shims).

Integration notes / friction points:
- Many teams have existing code that expects exact hosted API shapes (function-calling). Might need an adapter layer in the shim to translate or stub.
- Model weight formats: support load paths for ggml/gptq/gguf; need small loader wrapper that normalizes metadata (vocab, context_size).

Quick dev checklist (one-person MVP):
- [x] basic HTTP server with POST /v1/local/run and /v1/local/sessions (no persistence)
- [x] simple router to invoke external 'run_local_model.sh' with args and capture stdout as response
- [ ] session manager + disk KV persisting
- [ ] sharing / process reuse logic
- [ ] python shim for existing SDK (monkeypatch)

Notes to self: keep this lightweight. Aim for something I can demo in ~2 hours to a teammate: create session -> run prompt -> show cached repeat fast path. If it works, iterate to support docker backends and tiny web UI.

References / related:
- existing rw-serving runtime docs (confluence link placeholder)
- internal PR: github.com/redwood-inference/rw-adapters PR#207 (see linked_artifacts)

End of scratchpad. Will revisit on Monday after pairing with Maya.
